summary: Candidate A closely follows the frozen contract, while Candidate B changes the lower-level Add API and bypasses it from Upload.
reasons: A adds the exact Upload signature, explicitly validates empty filenames and nil readers, uses multipartbody.NewFile("file", fileName, content), and delegates to FilesService.Add.
A preserves Add unchanged, retaining its existing behavior, option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors.
A’s retry test uses io.MultiReader, providing meaningful coverage with non-seekable streamed content, and verifies that the replayed multipart payload remains intact.

A separately covers multipart field/name/content, pre-request validation, and source-reader error propagation as required by the contract. B omits dedicated validation and source-reader-error tests and replaces an existing basic Add test with changed semantics coverage instead of preserving it unchanged in scope intent.【Note: existing-suite passed, but visible test replacement reduces direct baseline clarity.】 B buffers every Add body, changes Add error semantics by wrapping read failures, introduces a duplicate private add path, and has Upload call that private path rather than the required existing Add method. B’s README and changelog explicitly advertise the out-of-scope Add behavior change.
risks_a: Validation tests check only that an error exists, not its exact message.
The first retry attempt returns 429 without explicitly consuming and checking the multipart body, though the second attempt verifies replayed content.
risks_b: Violates the requirement to preserve FilesService.Add behavior by eagerly reading and buffering all caller-provided bodies.
Changes Add source-reader errors to a new wrapped "read file body" error.

Upload bypasses Add, contrary to the required single path for options, request construction, decoding, and errors, and creates duplicate internal machinery through add(). Nit: currently same logic, but future divergence risk is real. B does not explicitly validate empty filenames or nil content before invoking the multipart helper, leaving contract fidelity dependent on undocumented helper behavior visible only by inference. Tests do not cover the required validation and source-reader-error cases. Documentation promotes the prohibited Add semantic change, expanding scope beyond the requested convenience API.
